title: Design by Contract
concept: Design by Contract is a software methodology where every function declares formal preconditions, postconditions, and invariants — making specifications executable.
why: DbC transforms software from 'it seems to work' to 'it provably works within these bounds.' It's the foundation of reliable systems programming.
tips: Write contracts FIRST — they clarify your thinking before you write implementation
A function without a contract is under-specified — you can't tell if it's working correctly
Contracts are the bridge between 'what the code does' and 'what the code SHOULD do'
DbC works at ALL levels: individual functions, type methods, FFI boundaries, system APIs
common_mistakes: Writing contracts AFTER the implementation — you just encode existing behavior, bugs and all
Treating contracts as optional — in DbC, they're as important as the implementation
Making contracts too weak to be useful — 'ensures: true' is technically correct but pointless
